en: An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the effort force needed to lift a heavy box by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
Applying oil to a rusty bicycle chain reduces friction between the metal parts, allowing the wheels to spin more freely with less pedaling effort.
When you drop a ball, Earth's gravity exerts an invisible downward pull on its mass, causing the ball to accelerate toward the ground.
Wrapping a copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that can pick up paperclips.
Rubbing a balloon on your hair transfers electrons to the balloon, giving it a negative charge that attracts positively charged pieces of paper.
When light travels from air into a glass of water, it slows down and bends, making a partially submerged straw look broken.
Striking a drum causes its tight skin to vibrate, pushing nearby air molecules to transmit sound waves to your ear.
Placing a metal spoon in hot soup causes vibrating soup molecules to collide with the spoon's atoms, transferring heat energy up the handle.
Releasing a stretched rubber band converts its stored potential energy into kinetic energy, causing the band to snap back to its original shape.
Pushing down on the long end of a seesaw lever creates a rotational force that lifts a heavy friend sitting on the short end.
Bringing the north pole of one bar magnet near the north pole of another causes their magnetic fields to repel and push apart.
Closing a switch in a simple circuit completes the path for electrons to flow from the battery, lighting up the connected bulb.
